title: fix(plugin-auth)!: saving the auth settings refuses to turn off the last way to sign in
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg4dtXyZ5LXdjKJLUCWRNk76)_

domain:server#2 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CXhZcHuALPAjkDCiiT

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：保存认证设置时，按「这次保存写完以后」的状态判断：如果邮箱/密码登录关着，又没有任何其他能用的登录方式（凭据齐全的社交或 OIDC 登录、已登记身份提供方的企业 SSO、手机号登录、宿主声明的登录交接），这次保存被拒，整批都不写入，字段下用中英日西四语说明先配好哪一种。同一次保存里既关邮箱/密码又关 Google 会被拒；同一次保存里填好 Google 再关邮箱/密码可以通过。设置服务的写入谓词入参多了一个 `batch` 字段，里面是这次保存的全部键值。
- 为什么改：#30202 实测：没配好 SSO 就关掉邮箱/密码，提示「设置已保存」，下次退出后所有人（包括管理员）都登不进来，只能改环境变量或数据库。契约复审还指出，逐键判断时，一次同时关掉邮箱/密码和 Google 的保存会被放行。
- 风险与回滚：只在保存门加一道拒收，不改已存的值，不改登录页和 `/auth/config`。这是收窄：以前能存下的「关掉最后一种登录方式」现在存不下；`batch` 是可选的新增字段，已有谓词不用改。已经锁死的部署用 `OS_AUTH_EMAIL_PASSWORD_ENABLED=true` 重启即可恢复。回滚即撤本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.ts` 的 `signInMethodFloorPredicate` 与 `googleAfter`（保存后的状态怎么算）、`otherSignInMethods`（哪些算其他登录方式）；`service-settings` 的 `refuseByWritePredicates`（`batch` 从哪来）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/sign-in-method-floor.test.ts` 预期 17/17；`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-settings exec vitest run src/settings-write-predicate.test.ts` 预期 9/9。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

Fixes #30202

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — a save an administrator could make before is now refused at the settings save door with the existing `SETTINGS_VALIDATION` / `invalid_value` field error: a save after which email and password is off and nothing else signs anyone in, judged on the whole save, including the Google change that removes the last provider while email and password is off. No new error code or settings key. The widening half: `SettingsWritePredicateInput`, exported from `@objectstack/service-settings`, gains an optional `batch` field, the whole write a predicate is asked about.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no file under `skills/**` teaches `auth.email_password_enabled` or the settings write predicate; `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx` already names the `OS_AUTH_EMAIL_PASSWORD_ENABLED` override the recovery uses.

## What changes

- **The refusal sits at the save door, before anything is written.** `bindAuthSettings` applies a value after it is stored, so a refusal there (the `refusable` pieces, #20412) would leave the console showing "saved" while the runtime ignores the value. The settings service already has the door for this: a write predicate (`SettingsService.registerWritePredicate`, the ADR-0144 D4 currency-lock seam), asked by `setMany` after the declared constraints and before any row or secret is written, refusing the whole batch with `SettingsValidationError` (`400 SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, `details.fields[]` ADR-0114 field errors). `AuthPlugin.bindAuthSettings` registers one predicate, from the new `sign-in-method-floor.ts`, on `auth.email_password_enabled`, `auth.google_enabled`, `auth.google_client_id` and `auth.google_client_secret`.
- **The whole save is judged (`service-settings`).** `SettingsWritePredicateInput` gains `batch?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>`: every key the write sets in the namespace, the asked key among them, with the value it would store (`null` clears). `refuseByWritePredicates` builds it once from the patch, frozen, and passes it to every predicate it asks. Optional, so a caller that builds an input by hand and every existing predicate (the currency lock) are unchanged. It is reachable from the package entry (`index.ts` re-exports the type; the built `dist/index.d.ts` carries `batch?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>`), pinned by an `expectTypeOf` case that imports it from `./index.js`.
- **The floor reads the state after the save.** Asked one key at a time against the configuration in force, `{ email_password_enabled: false, google_enabled: false }` on a deployment with email and password plus Google passed both keys, since each saw the other way in still standing, and wrote both (the review's must-fix). Now each key's value after the save is: the environment override when one is in force for it (it wins over what is saved); else the batch's value; else the value as it stands (the running configuration for `email_password_enabled`, the resolved setting for the `google_*` keys, read with `SettingsService.get`). A cleared key reads as its default (on, for both toggles), as `validatePatch`'s own post-write view does. Google after the save follows the rule the apply uses: off when `google_enabled` is off; else kept when declared at boot; else in force with a client ID and secret, each from the setting or its `GOOGLE_CLIENT_*` variable. A save that sets no `google_*` key leaves Google as it stands.
- **Where the refusal lands.** At `email_password_enabled` when the save turns it off and nothing is in force after it; at a `google_*` key when, with email and password off after the save, the save removes a Google provider that was in force and leaves nothing else. The batch above is refused at both keys.
- **What counts as another way in**, read live at save time from the running manager: the methods the login page still offers with email and password off, the same facts its "No sign-in method is available" state reads (`ui/packages/auth/src/LoginForm.tsx`, #29159), plus the one path the host states:
  - a social or OIDC provider in force (`getPublicConfig().socialProviders`) **whose client ID and client secret are both non-blank** in the configuration it came from (the review's should-fix). `AuthPlugin` indexes the providers declared at boot (stack config, the `GOOGLE_CLIENT_*` fallback, `auth:configure` handlers) with `providerCredentialIndex`; Google added from the settings has a pair by construction, since the apply adds it only with both. A provider listed without them draws a button that signs nobody in;
  - enterprise SSO switched on (`plugins.sso` / `OS_SSO_ENABLED`) AND at least one `sys_sso_provider` row, read with the boot report's `probeSsoProvidersPresence`. The switch alone signs nobody in, and an unreadable table proves no row, so neither counts;
  - phone-number sign-in (`features.phoneNumber`): better-auth's `/sign-in/phone-number` does not check `emailAndPassword.enabled`, and the code sign-in works when SMS can deliver;
  - a host sign-in handoff the host declared (`AuthPluginOptions.hostSignInHandoff`).
  - Not counted: `ssoOnlyMode` alone (it says an identity provider is in front; that provider is one of the above or nothing), and magic link and passkeys, which no login page offers (`PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES_NOT_ADVERTISED`, #7481).
- **The refusal.** `code: invalid_value` at the key, `constraint: { lastSignInMethod: 'email_password' | 'google' }`, and a message in the caller's language (`en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES`, the settings bundle's locales, picked with `resolveLocale` as the currency lock does) saying to keep or set up another sign-in method before or in that save. Turning email and password on, clearing it (its default is on), or re-saving a value in force is never refused.
- **Recovery for a deployment already locked out.** No new variable: `OS_AUTH_EMAIL_PASSWORD_ENABLED=true` is the settings env override for the key, it wins over the stored `false` (source `env`), and the apply turns email and password back on at the next boot. Named in the changeset and pinned below; the refusal message speaks to the administrator in Setup, who is not locked out, so it names what to configure instead.
- The edits in `auth-plugin.ts`: the import, the registration at the top of `bindAuthSettings`, and one field (`bootProviderCredentials`) set beside `configuredSocialProviders` after `auth:configure`, clear of the `mfa_required` and `allowed_ip_ranges` hunks and of `isExplicit`.
- `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`: one row for the new test's `findOne` double, written by `check-engine-double-contract.mjs --write` (outside the claimed file surface; the gate requires it for a new test file with an engine double).
- Changeset `.changeset/30202-keep-a-sign-in-method.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/service-settings`, both `patch`.

## Tests

`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.test.ts` (new, 17 cases). The real `SettingsService` (aliased to `service-settings/src` by this package's vitest config), the real `AuthPlugin` and `AuthManager`; a stub engine answers `sys_sso_provider` from each case's rows.

1. Email and password off with nothing else: `setMany` rejects with `SettingsValidationError` (`SETTINGS_VALIDATION`), one field error at `email_password_enabled` (`invalid_value`, `lastSignInMethod: email_password`); the stored value stays the default `true`, a sibling in the same batch (`password_min_length`) is not written, the manager keeps email and password on; turning it on is accepted.
2. The HTTP door, through `registerSettingsRoutes`: `PUT /api/settings/auth` with `Accept-Language: zh-CN` answers `400`, `error.code: SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, the field error at the key, its message the `zh-CN` copy.
3. Each way in that counts lets it turn off (stack-config GitHub, phone-number sign-in, host handoff, SSO with a registered provider; and Google saved on the page first).
4. The SSO switch with no provider row, and with a provider table that throws, is refused.
5. With email and password off and Google the last way in: `google_enabled: false`, `google_client_secret: null` and `google_client_id: ''` are each refused (`lastSignInMethod: google`), Google stays in force; with email and password back on, Google can go.
6. The same Google change is accepted where a stack-config GitHub keeps a way in, and a cleared secret that `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` still supplies is accepted and removes nothing.
7. Recovery: a `false` stored before the predicate exists rules at the next boot (control), and with `OS_AUTH_EMAIL_PASSWORD_ENABLED=true` in the settings env the manager has email and password on.
8. The whole save: `{ email_password_enabled: false, google_enabled: false }` and `{ email_password_enabled: false, google_client_secret: null }`, with email and password plus Google in force, are each refused with exactly two field errors (`email_password_enabled` / `email_password`, the Google key / `google`); nothing is written and both stay on.
9. Google filled in (`google_enabled`, client ID and secret) in the same save as `email_password_enabled: false` is accepted: email and password off, Google on.
10. `{ google_enabled: true, email_password_enabled: false }` over a client ID and secret already stored is accepted (the pair is read as stored).
11. `{ google_enabled: true, google_client_id, email_password_enabled: false }` with no secret anywhere is refused at `email_password_enabled`.
12. A stack-config GitHub listed with a blank secret is no way in: email and password off is refused.
13. `providerCredentialIndex` keys social and OIDC boot providers by whether both credentials are set.

`packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-write-predicate.test.ts` (+2): `setMany` hands a predicate the whole write as `batch`, frozen, a clear as `null`; and `SettingsWritePredicateInput['batch']`, imported from the package entry, is `Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> | undefined`.

## Acceptance notes

- **A cleared key reads as its default.** Clearing a key at organization scope can fall back to a global row rather than the default; the floor, like `validatePatch`'s post-write view, reads the default (on, for both toggles). Measured cases do not reach it; named so a review can weigh it.
- **The ui half (`domain:ui`, the lane is off duty; for the seat to file).** The Setup page shows no confirmation before the switch and shows the refusal only as the field error the console's extractor already reads. The card also saw the login page draw the email and password form under `os dev`, with better-auth's English "Email and password is not enabled" on submit; at `797f9257` `LoginForm.tsx` has the no-method state from #29257 (`noSignInMethod`, :351), so the remaining shape is what the console dev server draws there. Not reproduced here.
- **Other doors to the same lockout, not covered (read, not measured).** Deleting the last `sys_sso_provider` row, or a redeploy that drops the last stack-config provider or `plugins.phoneNumber`, while email and password is off. They are not settings saves, so this predicate cannot see them.
- **Dogfood reds that were not this change.** On the first head, `permission-set-clone-door.dogfood.test.ts` was `main`'s red #30255 (reverted by #30262; red with the floor neutralized too). On this head, four `package-commit-revert-path-package.dogfood.test.ts` cases timed out at 5000 ms while the 73 gate families ran beside the battery; the same file alone under the lock passes 12/12.
- `/auth/config` and the login page are unchanged: `emailPassword.enabled` reports the runtime truthfully.

## Verification
